name: flutter-intercept
description: Inspect, pause, edit, block and mock your Flutter app's HTTP traffic — no code in your app, no setup. Just press F5.

flutterIntercept.enabled.description: Route the HTTP traffic of Dart/Flutter debug sessions through Flutter Intercept. When off, debug sessions are launched untouched.

flutterIntercept.port.description: Port of the local intercepting proxy. If it is busy the next free port (up to 8999) is used.

flutterIntercept.captureSource.description: Record where in your code each request was made (a stack trace sent out of band to the proxy), so you can jump from a request to its source line. Takes effect on the next launch. Flutter sessions only (plain Dart programs always record).

flutterIntercept.upstreamProxy.description: Send intercepted traffic on through another HTTP proxy (for example Charles or Burp at http://127.0.0.1:8888, or a corporate proxy). Empty = connect to servers directly.

flutterIntercept.upstreamProxyIgnoreCert.description: Accept any certificate from servers reached through the upstream proxy. Needed only when that proxy decrypts HTTPS itself (Charles, Burp). Leave off otherwise.

flutterIntercept.tlsPassthrough.markdownDescription: Hosts (globs on the hostname, e.g. `*.bank.example`) whose HTTPS is passed through **without decryption**, for apps that pin certificates themselves (Dio `validateCertificate`, native pinning). Their connections are listed as tunnels; rules other than block don't apply.

host.description: Hostname glob, optionally with :port (e.g. api.corp.example or *.corp.example:8443).

cert.description: Path to a PEM certificate (with key).

key.description: Path to the PEM private key (with cert).

flutterIntercept.clientCertificates.markdownDescription: Client certificates the proxy presents to servers that require mutual TLS. Paths are absolute or relative to the workspace. Passphrases are kept in VS Code's secret storage: run **Flutter Intercept: Set Client Certificate Passphrase…**.

flutterIntercept.web.enabled.description: Also intercept Flutter Web apps launched in Chrome from VS Code (the browser is started with Flutter Intercept as its proxy). The web-server device can't be intercepted.

enumDescriptions: Show requests from native HTTP clients (cupertino_http, cronet_http, ok_http) read-only, from the app's HTTP profile.

Also route native clients through Flutter Intercept on Android emulators (debug sessions; the emulator's global proxy is restored when the session ends). HTTPS needs the app's debug network_security_config to trust the Flutter Intercept CA (Flutter Intercept: Save CA Certificate…). Elsewhere the same as profile.
Don't read the app's HTTP profile.
flutterIntercept.nativeClients.description: Requests made by native HTTP clients bypass the proxy, so they can't be mocked or paused. With "profile", they are still listed (read-only) from the app's HTTP profile in debug and profile mode.

enumDescriptions: Route requests from background isolates (compute, Isolate.run, Isolate.spawn) through Flutter Intercept too, in debug mode.
Only warn that requests from background isolates are not intercepted.
flutterIntercept.backgroundIsolates.description: HttpOverrides applies per isolate, so requests from background isolates normally bypass the proxy. With "intercept", Flutter Intercept installs its overrides in each new isolate of an intercepted debug session before it runs.

enumDescriptions: Notify when a request fails (network error or a 5xx response).
flutterIntercept.notifications.description: Show a notification when the app's requests fail while the traffic panel is not visible. At most one notification every 10 seconds; mocked, blocked and simulated failures are not reported.

flutterIntercept.contractCheck.description: Check JSON responses against your json_serializable / freezed models (their generated *.g.dart) and show fields that would make fromJson throw, such as a null in a non-nullable field.

flutterIntercept.rewriteLocalhost.description: Send requests the app makes to the emulator host aliases (10.0.2.2, 10.0.3.2) to this machine's localhost. localhost and 127.0.0.1 already reach this machine through the proxy. Never applies to physical iPhones (LAN mode).

enumDescriptions: AI agents can read traffic and add mocks/blocks/breakpoints (every change is confirmed by the agent client).
AI agents can only read traffic.
flutterIntercept.agent.access.description: What AI agents (Copilot agent mode, Claude Code, Cursor, other MCP clients) may do.

flutterIntercept.agent.redactSecrets.description: Hide Authorization, cookies, API keys, tokens and passwords from AI agents (tool results and HAR exports). The app always receives the real values.

flutterIntercept.agent.screenshots.description: Let AI agents take screenshots of the running app (take_screenshot). Each screenshot asks for your confirmation first.

flutterIntercept.agent.mcpPort.description: Port of the local MCP server for AI agents (listens on 127.0.0.1 only). If it is busy, the next free port is used.

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_get_status
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: Intercept status
languageModelTools.userDescription: Show proxy, session and traffic status.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Get Flutter Intercept status: whether the intercepting proxy runs, the running debug sessions (device, program), how many requests are recorded and paused, the agent access level, and warnings about traffic that is NOT intercepted (e.g. requests from a background isolate, native HTTP clients that are only listed read-only, requests that bypass the proxy). Also: upstreamProxy (host:port the traffic is chained through; upstreamProxySource "http.proxy" = VS Code's proxy setting), tlsPassthrough (host globs whose HTTPS is passed through undecrypted, listed as kind "tunnel") and clientCertificates ([{host, loaded, problem?}] — mutual-TLS certificates the proxy presents; a problem means it did not load and the server will likely reject the connection). Call this first to see whether an app is running before using the other tools.

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_list_requests
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: List HTTP requests
languageModelTools.userDescription: List recorded HTTP requests.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: List HTTP requests the running Flutter/Dart app made (newest first), recorded by Flutter Intercept's proxy. Filter by URL glob (* matches any characters), method, status (code, class like "4xx", or "error"), state, start time, kind ("websocket", "sse", "http"), GraphQL operation name, or slowerThanMs (only requests that took longer). Items show kind, the GraphQL operation and captured: "vm-profile" for read-only requests of native HTTP clients (no rules apply to them); kind "tunnel" items are TLS connections to a flutterIntercept.tlsPassthrough host, passed through undecrypted (notDecrypted: true, bytesSent / bytesReceived, no status, headers or bodies). Returns ids; call get_request for headers and bodies, get_frames for WebSocket messages / SSE events. Secrets are redacted.

url.description: URL glob on the full URL; * matches any characters (e.g. "https://api.example.com/v1/users*", "*/users/*"). Matched against the URL as you see it (redacted query values read "[redacted]").

method.description: HTTP method (case-insensitive). Omit to match any method.

status.description: An exact status code, a class ("2xx".."5xx"), or "error" (failed/aborted exchanges).

sinceMs.description: Only exchanges that started at or after this time (epoch milliseconds).

kind.description: "websocket", "sse" (server-sent events), "tunnel" (a TLS connection passed through undecrypted for a flutterIntercept.tlsPassthrough host) or "http" (everything else).

graphqlOperation.description: Only GraphQL requests with this operation name (exact, case-sensitive).

includeBrowserInternal.description: Flutter Web: also include the browser's own requests (Chrome updates, GCM, optimization guide), which are hidden by default.

slowerThanMs.description: Only finished requests that took longer than this many milliseconds (durationMs > slowerThanMs). Read where the time went with get_request (timings).

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_get_request
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: Get HTTP request details
languageModelTools.userDescription: Show one request with headers and bodies.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Get one recorded HTTP exchange by id: method, URL, status, request/response headers and decoded bodies (long bodies truncated, binary bodies summarised, secrets redacted), error, and timings (ms per phase: requestMs = receiving the app's request, pausedMs = held at breakpoints, delayMs = added by a mock delay / throttle, dnsMs / connectMs / tlsMs on a new upstream connection or reused: true, sendMs, waitMs = time to first byte from the server, receiveMs = downloading the response; a missing phase did not happen or is unknown). scriptLog holds the lines a user's script rule logged (redacted). Use after list_requests or wait_for_request. Pass snippet ("curl", "dart_http" or "dio") to also get the request as runnable code (redacted values stay "[redacted]"). For large JSON responses prefer get_body_shape first. Also shows kind (websocket/sse), frameCount (read the frames with get_frames), graphql {operationName, operationType}, cors (a browser preflight / why a browser would block the response, Flutter Web) and captured: "vm-profile" (read-only, from a native HTTP client). A tunnel (kind "tunnel") has no headers or bodies: tunnel {notDecrypted: why, bytesSent, bytesReceived} explains that the host is passed through without decryption (usually because the app pins its certificate) — remove it from flutterIntercept.tlsPassthrough to inspect it. clientCertificate is the host pattern of the mutual-TLS client certificate the proxy presented upstream. multipart/form-data bodies are shown parsed: secret fields "[redacted]", file parts "[file <name>, N bytes]".

maxBodyChars.description: Bodies longer than this are cut and marked truncated.

snippet.description: Also return the request as code: "curl", "dart_http" (package:http) or "dio". Built from the redacted view.

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_wait_for_request
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: Wait for an HTTP request
languageModelTools.userDescription: Wait for a matching request to complete.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Wait until the app makes a request matching a URL glob (and optional method/status) and it completes, then return it. Use this right after triggering an action to verify the resulting network call. After hot_restart or launch_app you can call wait_for_request directly: requests sent since the restart/launch are included, even if they finished before this call. Otherwise only requests starting after this call count (pass sinceMs to choose). Returns the sinceMs it used, and {timedOut: true} after timeoutMs (default 30 s, max 120 s).

url.description: URL glob on the full URL; * matches any characters (e.g. "https://api.example.com/v1/users*", "*/users/*"). Matched against the URL as you see it (redacted query values read "[redacted]").

method.description: HTTP method (case-insensitive). Omit to match any method.

status.description: An exact status code, a class ("2xx".."5xx"), or "error" (failed/aborted exchanges).

sinceMs.description: Only exchanges that started at or after this time (epoch ms), or "now" = when this call starts. Default: the start of the latest launch_app/hot_restart if it was within the last 120 s (so requests the app sent since then count), otherwise "now".

anyOf.description: Only exchanges that started at or after this time (epoch milliseconds).

timeoutMs.description: Give up after this long (max 120000) and return {timedOut: true}.

includeBrowserInternal.description: Flutter Web: also include the browser's own requests (Chrome updates, GCM, optimization guide), which are hidden by default.

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_list_paused
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: List paused requests
languageModelTools.userDescription: List requests paused at a breakpoint.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: List exchanges currently paused by a breakpoint rule, with their phase (request or response) and the time they auto-resume. Resume or abort them with resume_request / abort_request.

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_list_rules
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: List intercept rules
languageModelTools.userDescription: List mock, block and breakpoint rules.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: List the active intercept rules (mocks, blocks, breakpoints, …) in priority order: the first enabled matching rule wins. Rules created by agents are named "[agent] ...". Script rules (the user's own JavaScript hooks) are shown as {kind: "script", file?} without their code; agents cannot read, add or change scripts.

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_export_har
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: Export HAR
languageModelTools.userDescription: Export recorded traffic to a HAR file.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Export recorded exchanges (optionally filtered by URL, method, start time) as a HAR 1.2 file under the project's .dart_tool/flutter_intercept/exports/ and return its path. Secrets are redacted according to the user's setting.

url.description: URL glob on the full URL; * matches any characters (e.g. "https://api.example.com/v1/users*", "*/users/*"). Matched against the URL as you see it (redacted query values read "[redacted]").

method.description: HTTP method (case-insensitive). Omit to match any method.

sinceMs.description: Only exchanges that started at or after this time (epoch milliseconds).

includeBrowserInternal.description: Flutter Web: also include the browser's own requests (Chrome updates, GCM, optimization guide), which are hidden by default.

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_get_request_source
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: Find the code that sent a request
languageModelTools.userDescription: Show the Dart call site that sent a request.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Find where in the app's Dart code a recorded request was made. Returns appFrame (the app's call site: function, package URI, path relative to the project, line, column) and the stack frames (inProject marks the project's own files; afterAsyncGap marks frames after an await). Use it to go from an unexpected, failing or duplicated request straight to the code that sent it. Returns {available: false, reason} when there is no trace: source capture off, a request sent by the editor/an agent, or the trace has not arrived yet (retry shortly).

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_get_body_shape
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: Get JSON body structure
languageModelTools.userDescription: Show the structure of a JSON body.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Get the structure of a recorded JSON response (or request, which:"request") body without its values: key names and types only, every array merged into one element shape plus its length. Compact even for megabyte bodies, so use it before get_request to understand an API response or to write/fix model classes and parsing code. Notation: "string" | "integer" | "number" | "boolean" | "null"; unions like "string|null"; "key?" = missing in some merged objects; arrays {"[]": element shape, "length": n or "min-max"}; {"|": [...]} = a union mixing objects/arrays; "{…}" / "[…]" = deeper than maxDepth; "…" = more keys omitted. Non-JSON bodies return {shape: null, reason}.

maxDepth.description: Nesting depth to describe (1-12); deeper structure shows as "{…}" / "[…]".

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_check_contract
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: Check responses against the Dart models
languageModelTools.userDescription: Check JSON responses against the Dart models.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Check recorded JSON responses against the app's own Dart models — exactly what the generated fromJson (json_serializable / freezed *.g.dart) would do with them. Finds the fields that would make parsing throw (error: a null or missing non-nullable field, a string where an int is expected, an unknown enum value) or are suspicious (warning). Pass id for one exchange, or url/method/sinceMs for the latest matching ones; model forces a model class. Each result says which model was used and how it was found (via: retrofit/chopper annotations, the request's stack trace, or the user's choice), or checked:false with the reason (no model mapped, not JSON, …). Violations give the JSON path, the model field, expected vs actual type and the model file:line (project-relative). Use it when the app shows a parse error ("type 'Null' is not a subtype of type 'String'") or after changing a model.

id.description: Check this one exchange. Omit to check the latest matching JSON responses.

url.description: URL glob on the full URL; * matches any characters (e.g. "https://api.example.com/v1/users*", "*/users/*"). Matched against the URL as you see it (redacted query values read "[redacted]").

method.description: HTTP method (case-insensitive). Omit to match any method.

sinceMs.description: Only exchanges that started at or after this time (epoch milliseconds).

model.description: Check against this Dart model class (e.g. "User") instead of the one found automatically.

limit.description: Max exchanges to check when no id is given (newest first), 1-50.

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_generate_model
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: Generate Dart models from traffic
languageModelTools.userDescription: Generate Dart models from recorded responses.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Generate Dart model classes from the app's recorded JSON responses: every recorded sample of the same method + route is merged (a field missing in some samples becomes optional, a field seen null becomes nullable, int+double becomes double), nested objects get their own classes. Style follows the project (freezed, json_serializable or plain fromJson/toJson) unless style is given. Returns {files: [{path, content}], samples, route}: nothing is written, so write the files yourself (paths are suggestions relative to the project) and run build_runner for freezed/json_serializable. Secret field values are redacted before inference. Make the app call the endpoint a few times with different data first for better nullability.

id.description: A recorded exchange; every recorded response of the same method + route (e.g. GET /users/{id}) is used as a sample.

url.description: Or: the newest matching JSON response picks the route; all its recorded samples are used.

name.description: Root class name (default: from the URL, e.g. "User" for /users/{id}).

style.description: Code style. Default: the project's own (freezed > json_serializable > plain, from pubspec.yaml).

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_generate_fixture_test
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: Generate a fixture test from traffic
languageModelTools.userDescription: Generate JSON fixtures and a test from recorded requests.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Turn recorded exchanges into a test: one JSON fixture file per response under test/fixtures/ plus a test file that serves them with the project's mocking library (http_mock_adapter for Dio, package:http's MockClient, or mocktail for a Retrofit interface). Pass ids or a url glob. Returns {files: [{path, content}]} without writing them; adjust the generated test to call your repository/service and assert what matters. Always built from the redacted view: secrets appear as "[redacted]".

ids.description: Recorded exchanges to turn into fixtures (1-20).

url.description: Or: the newest (up to 20) finished exchanges matching this URL.

style.description: Test style. Default: the project's own dev_dependencies (http_mock_adapter > mocktail > mock_client).

name.description: snake_case base name for the files (default: from the first request, e.g. "get_user").

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_assert_traffic
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: Assert on recorded traffic
languageModelTools.userDescription: Check that expected requests and responses happened.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Check in one call that the app made the expected requests: matching url (glob; * matches any characters) and method since sinceMs (default: the latest launch_app/hot_restart, else all recorded traffic), with expect: status (code, "2xx".., "error"), count {min, max, exact} (default: at least one), order (URL globs requested in that order), json assertions on every matched response ({path: "$.items[0].id", exists | equals | type}), maxDurationMs. withinMs waits (event-driven, max 120 s) for the requests to arrive; it never hangs. Returns {pass, matched, ids, failures: [readable reasons]}. Failure texts name the request, path and expectation but never echo response values; equals compares with the redacted view (a secret only equals "[redacted]"). Use it as the final check of a change instead of reading bodies by hand.

url.description: Requests to check: a glob on the full URL; * matches any characters.

method.description: HTTP method (case-insensitive). Omit to match any method.

sinceMs.description: Only requests that started at or after this time (epoch ms). Default: the start of the latest launch_app/hot_restart if within the last 120 s, otherwise all recorded traffic.

withinMs.description: Wait up to this long (max 120000) for the expected requests. 0 = check what is recorded now. With count.max or count.exact the whole window is observed.

status.description: Every matched request has this status: a code, a class ("2xx".."5xx") or "error".

count.description: How many matching requests. Default: at least one.

order.description: URL globs that must have been requested in this order (each one starting after the previous one), among all requests since sinceMs.

items.description: URL glob on the full URL; * matches any characters (e.g. "https://api.example.com/v1/users*", "*/users/*"). Matched against the URL as you see it (redacted query values read "[redacted]").

path.description: JSON path into the response body: "$.user.avatar_url", "$.items[0].id", "$.items[*].price" ([*] = every element), "$['odd key']". No filters or "..".

exists.description: true: the path selects at least one value; false: it selects nothing. Default true when neither equals nor type is given.

equals.description: Every selected value deep-equals this JSON value. Compared with what get_request shows: a secret field only equals "[redacted]".

type.description: Every selected value has this JSON type ("integer" = a whole number).

items.description: An assertion on the JSON response body of every matched request.

maxDurationMs.description: Every matched request finished within this many ms.

expect.description: What must hold. Every given expectation is checked.

includeBrowserInternal.description: Flutter Web: also include the browser's own requests (Chrome updates, GCM, optimization guide), which are hidden by default.

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_get_frames
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: Get WebSocket / SSE frames
languageModelTools.userDescription: Show the messages of a WebSocket or SSE stream.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Read the messages of a recorded WebSocket connection or the events of a server-sent events (SSE) stream (list_requests kind "websocket" / "sse"): oldest first, each with index, dir ("send" = app → server, "receive"), at (epoch ms), kind (text, binary, ping, pong, close, event), size and text (SSE: event name and id). Binary payloads are summarised as "[binary N bytes]"; JSON messages are redacted structurally, other text by pattern (secrets read "[redacted]"). Page with since = the returned next; while the connection is open (state "pending") new frames keep arriving. Only the newest 500 frames per connection are kept (dropped counts the older ones).

since.description: Return frames from this index on (the `next` of the previous call). Indexes count every frame of the connection, including dropped ones. Default: the oldest kept frame.

maxChars.description: Each frame's text is cut to this many characters (marked truncated).

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_list_recordings
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: List traffic recordings
languageModelTools.userDescription: List saved traffic recordings.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: List the saved traffic recordings (id, name, createdAt, number of exchanges, whether secrets were redacted) and which one is being replayed, if any. Recordings are made with save_recording or from the traffic panel and live in the project's .dart_tool/flutter_intercept/recordings/ (not committed).

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_diff_recordings
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: Compare two recordings
languageModelTools.userDescription: Compare two traffic recordings.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Compare two recordings route by route (method + path template such as GET /users/{id}): routes added or removed, status changes, JSON shape changes (keys added/removed, type changes), how many body values changed (values are never shown), call-count changes and responses more than 2x slower. Use it to see what a backend or app change did to the traffic: save a recording before and after, then diff them (a = before, b = after). Details are redacted.

b.description: The recording to compare with it.

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_get_auth_flows
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: Analyse token refresh flows
languageModelTools.userDescription: Show 401 → token refresh → retry flows.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Find the app's token refresh flows in the recorded traffic: each 401/403, the refresh call(s) that followed and the retried request(s), with a stampede warning when the app sent several refresh calls for one expiry within 2 s, and a problem when the retry never happened or got 401 again. Steps carry exchange ids, method, redacted URL and status (read them with get_request). Combine with expire_token to test the refresh logic: expire_token, trigger the flow, then get_auth_flows.

sinceMs.description: Only exchanges that started at or after this time (epoch milliseconds).

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_export_openapi
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: Export OpenAPI from traffic
languageModelTools.userDescription: Export recorded traffic as an OpenAPI document.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Write an OpenAPI 3.1 document (JSON) inferred from the app's recorded HTTP traffic (optionally filtered by url glob, method, start time) under the project's .dart_tool/flutter_intercept/exports/ and return its path: servers per origin, paths with {id} parameters for id-like segments, query parameters, request and response bodies per status with JSON schemas inferred from every sample (required = present in all samples, nullable when seen null) and one example each. Returns {path, exchanges, routes, notes}. Use it to document an undocumented backend or to compare the app's real usage with a spec. Secrets are redacted according to the user's setting. Make the app call each endpoint a few times first for better schemas.

url.description: Only exchanges whose URL matches this glob (e.g. "https://api.example.com/v1/*"). Omit for every finished HTTP request.

method.description: HTTP method (case-insensitive). Omit to match any method.

sinceMs.description: Only exchanges that started at or after this time (epoch milliseconds).

title.description: Document / collection title. Default: the Flutter project's name.

includeBrowserInternal.description: Flutter Web: also include the browser's own requests (Chrome updates, GCM, optimization guide), which are hidden by default.

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_export_postman
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: Export Postman collection from traffic
languageModelTools.userDescription: Export recorded traffic as a Postman collection.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Write a Postman Collection v2.1 (JSON) from the app's recorded HTTP traffic (optionally filtered by url glob, method, start time) under the project's .dart_tool/flutter_intercept/exports/ and return its path: a folder per host, one request per route (the latest sample) with saved example responses, {{baseUrl}} variables per origin, and credential headers as empty {{variables}}. Returns {path, exchanges, routes, notes}. Secrets are redacted according to the user's setting.

url.description: Only exchanges whose URL matches this glob (e.g. "https://api.example.com/v1/*"). Omit for every finished HTTP request.

method.description: HTTP method (case-insensitive). Omit to match any method.

sinceMs.description: Only exchanges that started at or after this time (epoch milliseconds).

title.description: Document / collection title. Default: the Flutter project's name.

includeBrowserInternal.description: Flutter Web: also include the browser's own requests (Chrome updates, GCM, optimization guide), which are hidden by default.

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_take_screenshot
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: Take a screenshot of the app
languageModelTools.userDescription: Take a screenshot of the running app (asks first).
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Take a screenshot of the running Flutter app (the debug session's device; pass sessionId when several apps run) to see what the UI shows after a change or a mocked response. Returns the PNG image plus {path, width, height, takenAt, method, recentRequests}: recentRequests are the (at most 10) requests that started in the 5 s before the screenshot (redacted summaries; read them with get_request). The user confirms every screenshot and can turn the tool off (setting flutterIntercept.agent.screenshots). Supported on Android devices/emulators, iOS simulators, macOS and Flutter Web in Chrome (and wherever the Flutter VM service can render one); other devices answer "not supported".

sessionId.description: Debug session to capture (see get_status). Omit when exactly one app is running.

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_add_mock
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: Add mock rule
languageModelTools.userDescription: Add a rule that answers matching requests with a fake response.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Make the app receive a fake response for matching requests (the real server is not contacted). Use it to test error states and edge cases (e.g. status 500, empty lists, slow responses via delayMs) without touching the backend. The rule is inserted first so it wins. Pass times (e.g. 1 = only the next request, to test a retry) or ttlMs to have it removed automatically; otherwise remove it with remove_rule when done. GraphQL: all operations share one URL, so pass graphqlOperation (e.g. "GetUser") to mock just that operation (list_requests shows the names). Refused: HTML / JavaScript / SVG content types (or an untyped HTML body), and 3xx redirects whose location leaves the request's own origin (except to localhost).

url.description: URL glob on the full URL; * matches any characters (e.g. "https://api.example.com/v1/users*", "*/users/*"). Matched against the URL as you see it (redacted query values read "[redacted]").

method.description: HTTP method (case-insensitive). Omit to match any method.

graphqlOperation.description: Only GraphQL requests with this operation name (exact, case-sensitive), e.g. "GetUser". The url glob still applies (usually the GraphQL endpoint, e.g. "*/graphql").

headers.description: Response headers. content-type defaults to application/json when body is an object.

body.description: Response body: text, or a JSON object/array (sent as JSON).

name.description: Optional label; it is shown as "[agent] <name>" in the rules list.

times.description: Apply the rule to the first N matching requests only (1-1000); it is then removed automatically.

ttlMs.description: Remove the rule automatically after this many milliseconds (1000-86400000).

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_add_block
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: Add block rule
languageModelTools.userDescription: Add a rule that blocks matching requests.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Block matching requests: answer with a status (default 403) or reset the connection (mode "reset") to simulate a network failure. languageModelTools.modelDescription: Start the Flutter/Dart app in a normal VS Code debug session; Flutter Intercept routes its HTTP traffic through the proxy automatically. Optional deviceId (see get_status / the selected device), program (e.g. lib/main_dev.dart) and flutterMode (debug or profile). Returns {sessionId, sinceMs} once the session started; then call wait_for_request directly — requests the app sent since the launch are included.

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_hot_restart
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: Hot restart Flutter app
languageModelTools.userDescription: Hot restart the running app.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Hot-restart the running app (or all intercepted sessions) so it starts over with the current code and rules; interception stays on. Returns {restarted, sinceMs}. Then call wait_for_request directly to verify the network calls made at startup: requests sent since the restart are included, even ones that finished before wait_for_request was called.

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_simulate_network
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: Simulate network conditions (all app traffic or matching requests)
languageModelTools.userDescription: Throttle or break the network for the app or for matching requests.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Simulate bad network conditions to test loading states, timeouts, retries and offline handling. Without url: set the profile for ALL app traffic: "slow-3g", "fast-3g", "flaky" (20% of requests fail), "offline" (every request fails), "custom" (latencyMs, kbps, uploadKbps, dropRate), or "none" to restore normal speed (do this when done). With url (a glob; * matches any characters): add a rule, inserted first, that slows only matching requests with the given profile, or makes them fail with fault ("reset", "timeout", "truncate", "dns"); times / ttlMs remove the rule automatically, otherwise use remove_rule. Mocks and blocks still answer instantly. get_status shows the active profile; affected exchanges carry a "simulated" label.

profile.description: "slow-3g" (+400 ms, 400 kbps down / 400 up), "fast-3g" (+150 ms, 1600 kbps down / 750 up), "flaky" (+200 ms, 20% of requests fail), "offline" (every request fails), "custom" (use latencyMs/kbps/uploadKbps/dropRate), "none" (restore). Required unless `fault` is given.

latencyMs.description: custom: added latency per request, ms.

kbps.description: custom: response bandwidth, kilobits per second.

uploadKbps.description: custom: request (upload) bandwidth, kilobits per second; also paces WebSocket messages the app sends.

dropRate.description: custom: share of requests that fail (0-1).

url.description: Only affect requests matching this URL glob (adds a rule, inserted first). Omit to set the profile for ALL app traffic.

method.description: HTTP method (case-insensitive). Omit to match any method.

graphqlOperation.description: With url: only GraphQL requests with this operation name (exact, case-sensitive).

fault.description: With url: make matching requests fail instead of slowing them: "reset" (connection reset), "timeout" (no answer until the client gives up), "truncate" (response cut mid-body), "dns" (lookup failure).

times.description: Apply the rule to the first N matching requests only (1-1000); it is then removed automatically.

ttlMs.description: Remove the rule automatically after this many milliseconds (1000-86400000).

name.description: Optional label; it is shown as "[agent] <name>" in the rules list.

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_resend_request
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: Resend a request
languageModelTools.userDescription: Send a recorded request again, optionally edited.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Send a recorded request again through the proxy, optionally edited (method, url, headers, body), without involving the app — e.g. to check a fix on the backend or try a different payload. Only for an app request that reached the real server unchanged (state "completed", no rule matched it, not from a physical device over LAN), and only to that request's own origin: edit.url may change path and query, never scheme, host or port. Anything else is refused with the reason. Omitted fields keep the original, including secret headers you only see as "[redacted]"; a "[redacted]" value in edit.headers (or the query) is replaced by the original. Rules and the network profile apply. Returns {id, sinceMs}: the new exchange starts "pending"; wait for it with wait_for_request (same url, that sinceMs) or check get_request(id).

method.description: HTTP method (case-insensitive). Omit to match any method.

url.description: Absolute http(s) URL with the SAME origin (scheme, host, port) as the recorded request; only path and query may change.

headers.description: Replaces the WHOLE header set. A value of "[redacted]" is replaced by the original value of that header.

body.description: New body text. Omit to keep the original body.

edit.description: Changes to the recorded request. Omit to send it unchanged.

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_add_mutation
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: Add response mutation rule
languageModelTools.userDescription: Add a rule that changes fields of real JSON responses.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Let matching requests reach the real server, then change its JSON response before the app gets it: ops [{path: "$.user.avatar_url", op: "null"}, {path: "$.items[*].price", op: "set", value: "9.99"}, {path: "$.email", op: "delete"}]. For an exact number form use valueJson (JSON text written byte-exact) instead of value: "1.0" to send a double (an int-typed Dart field then throws), integers beyond 2^53. Use it to reproduce or test how the app handles a null/missing/mistyped field from the backend (e.g. "Null is not a subtype of String") without mocking the whole response. Non-JSON responses pass unchanged. The rule is inserted first; times (e.g. 1) or ttlMs remove it automatically, otherwise use remove_rule. Affected exchanges carry a "simulated" label; check_contract shows what the models make of them.

url.description: URL glob on the full URL; * matches any characters (e.g. "https://api.example.com/v1/users*", "*/users/*"). Matched against the URL as you see it (redacted query values read "[redacted]").

method.description: HTTP method (case-insensitive). Omit to match any method.

graphqlOperation.description: Only GraphQL requests with this operation name (exact, case-sensitive), e.g. "GetUser". The url glob still applies (usually the GraphQL endpoint, e.g. "*/graphql").

path.description: JSON path into the response body: "$.user.avatar_url", "$.items[0].id", "$.items[*].price" ([*] = every element), "$['odd key']". No filters or "..".

op.description: "null" sets the field to null, "delete" removes the key (or array element), "set" replaces it with `value`.

value.description: With op "set": the new JSON value, e.g. "42" to send a number as a string. Max 1 MB.

valueJson.description: With op "set", instead of value: the new value as JSON text, written byte-exact. Use it when the exact number form matters: "1.0" (a double, which Dart parses as double, not int), integers beyond 2^53 ("12345678901234567890"), "1e3". Wins over value.

items.description: One change to the JSON response body.

ops.description: Changes applied in order to the real JSON response (1-20).

times.description: Apply the rule to the first N matching requests only (1-1000); it is then removed automatically.

ttlMs.description: Remove the rule automatically after this many milliseconds (1000-86400000).

name.description: Optional label; it is shown as "[agent] <name>" in the rules list.

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_add_cors_rule
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: Add CORS rule (development only)
languageModelTools.userDescription: Add a development-only rule that adds CORS headers to matching responses.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Flutter Web development only: let matching requests reach the real server, but answer the browser's CORS preflight (OPTIONS) locally and add Access-Control-Allow-Origin (default: the request's Origin; or allowOrigin), allow-methods/headers and optionally Allow-Credentials to the real response, so the app can be developed while the backend's CORS setup is wrong. By default only loopback pages (the Flutter Web dev server on localhost) are allowed, without credentials; pass allowOrigin / allowCredentials only when needed. The url must name a host. The real server is NOT changed: the same requests still fail in production until the backend sends the headers itself, so report the actual problem (get_request shows cors.problem). allowOrigin "*" cannot be combined with allowCredentials. Inserted first; times / ttlMs remove it automatically, otherwise use remove_rule.

url.description: URL glob WITH a host, e.g. "https://api.example.com/*" (match-all patterns such as "*" are refused).

method.description: HTTP method (case-insensitive). Omit to match any method.

allowOrigin.description: Access-Control-Allow-Origin to send: one origin such as "http://localhost:5000", or "*" (any website). Default: the request's Origin, but only for loopback pages (localhost, 127.0.0.1, [::1]). "null" is refused.

allowCredentials.description: Also allow credentials (cookies): Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. Default false. Not allowed with allowOrigin "*".

times.description: Apply the rule to the first N matching requests only (1-1000); it is then removed automatically.

ttlMs.description: Remove the rule automatically after this many milliseconds (1000-86400000).

name.description: Optional label; it is shown as "[agent] <name>" in the rules list.

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_save_recording
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: Save a traffic recording
languageModelTools.userDescription: Save the recorded traffic as a recording.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Save the finished HTTP exchanges and closed WebSocket / SSE streams with their messages (optionally only those matching url / since sinceMs; open connections, TLS tunnels and read-only native-client traffic are not recorded) as a named recording under the project's .dart_tool/flutter_intercept/recordings/. Secrets are saved as "[redacted]" unless you pass redact: false. Use recordings to replay a backend state offline (replay_recording: WebSocket / SSE streams replay as a scripted server with the recorded timing) or to compare traffic before and after a change (diff_recordings). Returns {id, name, exchanges, streams?, frames?} (streams = WebSocket / SSE exchanges among them).

name.description: A name for the recording, e.g. "checkout happy path".

url.description: Only exchanges whose URL matches this glob. Omit for every finished HTTP request and closed WebSocket / SSE stream.

sinceMs.description: Only exchanges that started at or after this time (epoch milliseconds).

redact.description: Save secrets (auth headers, cookies, tokens) as "[redacted]" (default true). Replays of a redacted recording send "[redacted]" values to the app.

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_replay_recording
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: Replay a recording
languageModelTools.userDescription: Answer requests from a saved recording (or stop replaying).
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Answer the app's requests from a saved recording instead of the real server: the same method + URL (and request body) gets the recorded response; several recorded responses for one request are served in order; requests whose path differs only in ids (/users/42 vs /users/7) match by path template. Rules still win. fallback decides what unmatched requests do: "passthrough" (real server, default) or "fail" (like offline — a fully offline demo). Recorded WebSocket / SSE streams are replayed too: the proxy answers the upgrade / stream itself and sends the recorded server messages with their timing (WebSocket: in step with the app's messages). Replayed exchanges carry simulated: "Replayed from <name>". Call it without id to stop replaying (do this when done); get_status / list_recordings show what is being replayed.

id.description: Recording to replay. Omit to stop replaying.

fallback.description: Requests the recording has no answer for: "passthrough" (go to the real server) or "fail" (fail like offline, for a fully offline demo).

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_add_sequence
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: Add a scenario (sequence) rule
languageModelTools.userDescription: Add a rule whose answer changes from request to request.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Make successive matching requests get different answers, to test retries, polling and recovery: steps [{kind:"mock", status:500, count:2}, {kind:"passthrough"}] fails the first two requests and lets the third reach the server. Step kinds: mock (status, body, headers, delayMs), block (status or reset), fault (reset, timeout, truncate, dns), throttle (latencyMs, kbps, uploadKbps, dropRate), passthrough (the real server); count = how many requests each step answers (default 1). then: "last" (default) keeps the last step, "passthrough", or "loop". Mock steps have add_mock's limits (no HTML/JavaScript, no redirects off the request's origin). The rule is inserted first; remove it with remove_rule when done. The panel and rule-hit show which step answered.

url.description: URL glob on the full URL; * matches any characters (e.g. "https://api.example.com/v1/users*", "*/users/*"). Matched against the URL as you see it (redacted query values read "[redacted]").

method.description: HTTP method (case-insensitive). Omit to match any method.

graphqlOperation.description: Only GraphQL requests with this operation name (exact, case-sensitive), e.g. "GetUser". The url glob still applies (usually the GraphQL endpoint, e.g. "*/graphql").

headers.description: Response headers. content-type defaults to application/json when body is an object.

body.description: Response body: text, or a JSON object/array (sent as JSON).

count.description: How many successive matching requests this step answers (1-1000, default 1).
How many successive matching requests this step answers (1-1000, default 1).
How many successive matching requests this step answers (1-1000, default 1).
How many successive matching requests this step answers (1-1000, default 1).
How many successive matching requests this step answers (1-1000, default 1).

steps.description: What successive matching requests get, in order (1-50 steps), e.g. [{kind:"mock", status:500, count:2}, {kind:"passthrough"}].

then.description: After the last step: "last" keeps answering with the last step (default), "passthrough" lets requests reach the server, "loop" starts over.

name.description: Optional label; it is shown as "[agent] <name>" in the rules list.

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_expire_token
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: Expire the auth token
languageModelTools.userDescription: Make matching requests fail with 401 "token expired" for a while.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Simulate an expired access token: the next count (default 1) requests matching url get 401 {"error":"token_expired"}; after that the real server answers again. Use it to test the app's token refresh: expire_token on the authenticated API, trigger a request, then get_auth_flows (did it refresh once and retry?) or assert_traffic. Inserted first; remove it with remove_rule when done.

url.description: URL glob of the authenticated request(s) whose token should look expired, e.g. "https://api.example.com/v1/*".

count.description: How many matching requests get 401 before the real server answers again (1-1000, default 1).

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_add_map_remote
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: Map requests to a local server
languageModelTools.userDescription: Send matching requests to a local server instead.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Redirect matching requests to a local backend (http://localhost:<port>, 127.0.0.1 or [::1], optionally with a path prefix): the path and query after the matched URL are kept, the app still sees the original URL, and exchanges carry simulated: "Mapped to <origin>". Requests keep their headers (including credentials), so map only to your own local server. Agents can only map to loopback targets; the user can map elsewhere from the panel. The url must name a host. Inserted first; remove it with remove_rule when done.

url.description: URL glob WITH a host of the requests to redirect, e.g. "https://api.example.com/*".

to.description: Loopback target origin or URL prefix: http://localhost:<port>, http://127.0.0.1:<port> or http://[::1]:<port> (optionally with a path prefix). Other hosts are refused for agents.

method.description: HTTP method (case-insensitive). Omit to match any method.

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_add_rewrite
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: Add a rewrite rule
languageModelTools.userDescription: Add a rule that changes headers, status or body text of real requests or responses.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Let matching requests reach the real server but change them on the way: request {setHeaders, removeHeaders, replaceBody} before forwarding, response {status, setHeaders, removeHeaders, replaceBody} before the app gets it. replaceBody is a literal find/replace on the decoded text (1-20 replacements, no regex). Use it for feature flags in headers, forcing a status, or patching a response text. Refused: setting request headers that carry credentials (Authorization, Cookie, *token*, *session*, *api-key* …); setting Location, Refresh, Set-Cookie, Content-Security-Policy, Access-Control-*, X-Forwarded-*, Forwarded, Host or method-override headers, or an HTML/JavaScript content-type; "[redacted]" values; request.replaceBody; markup or script in replacements; and — while secrets are redacted — response replaceBody (a find/replace could reveal redacted values); use add_mutation for JSON fields. The url must name a host. Inserted first; times / ttlMs remove it automatically, otherwise use remove_rule.

url.description: URL glob WITH a host, e.g. "https://api.example.com/v1/*".

method.description: HTTP method (case-insensitive). Omit to match any method.

graphqlOperation.description: Only GraphQL requests with this operation name (exact, case-sensitive), e.g. "GetUser". The url glob still applies (usually the GraphQL endpoint, e.g. "*/graphql").

setHeaders.description: Headers to set (replacing any existing value).

replace.description: Replacement text (at most 64 KB; all find + replace texts of a rule at most 256 KB).

all.description: Replace every occurrence (default: the first only).

replaceBody.description: Literal find/replace on the decoded text body, applied in order (1-20). Non-text bodies are left untouched.

request.description: Changes to the request before it is forwarded to the real server.

response.description: Changes to the real server's response before the app gets it.
